title: Japan's TEPCO to counter 'capacity squatters' in AI data center boom
key_facts: Tokyo Electric Power Co. Holdings (TEPCO) is among the Japanese utilities tightening rules on electricity for data centers.
The aim is to counter 'capacity squatting', which Nikkei describes as reserving power capacity that ends up underutilized.
Nikkei's standfirst says the new rules aim to prevent 'stranded capacity'.
A photo caption says Japanese utilities and authorities are struggling with huge power demand from data center projects that are often delayed, moved, or use less capacity than agreed.
quote_evidence: Tokyo Electric Power Co. Holdings is among the Japanese utilities tightening rules on electricity for data centers to counter a trend of operators "capacity squatting," or reserving power capacity that ends up being underutilized.
Tokyo power company's new rules aim to prevent stranded capacity
why_it_matters_hint: Power reserved for data centers that are delayed or never fully used can block others, so utilities are changing the rules.
notes: Nikkei Asia is behind a paywall: only the standfirst, the opening paragraph and a photo caption (about 500 characters) could be read, so fewer than 5 facts are available. No other outlet carried the story in Google News (three searches). The specific new rules (what operators must do, start date, fees) are not known.
